title: R’ Yudan bar Chanin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.10.1.14) where R’ Yudan transmits a teaching in the name of R’ Berechyah. A fine saying survives in [Orlah 1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Orlah.1.3.11): “A sign: one who eats from his fellow is ashamed to look at him.” This resembles [Berakhot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.6b.23-24): “Once a person depends on others, his face changes like the kerum.” He is also mentioned in legal discussions in [Pesachim 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.4.4.2) and [Kiddushin 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kiddushin.2.5.2), where R’ Yudan son of R’ Chanan says: “An ervah that is not an ervah takes hold of one that is not an ervah.”

notes.text: The checked Kiddushin text contains the difficult ervah formula. Its precise legal sense remains unresolved here; an unsupported legal paraphrase is not substituted. Chanin and Chanan remain distinct printed forms.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Kiddushin comparison contains the ervah formula, but no commentary resolving its legal referents was supplied. The Orlah phrase-search snippet is a lead rather than a fetched complete witness. Ashamed-to-look and kerum remain lexical readings, not proved source emendations; שנצטרך and the older machine שנצרך remain distinct recorded forms. Chanin and Chanan are not harmonized. All chapter/halakhah numbers, the Berakhot6b quotation and negations in the legal formula remain; uninspected abbreviated personal titles stay R’.

Orlah 1:3 gives the saying in the context of judging which tree sustains a graft. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud the name is Chanin in Orlah and Pesachim, and Chanan in Sanhedrin and Kiddushin. Berakhot 6b also explains kerum as a bird whose colors change. In Kiddushin 2:5 the preceding discussion concerns uncertain betrothal. Penei Moshe explains the difficult formula as a precaution: when the first betrothal may be invalid, a later betrothal may take effect and require a bill of divorce. Guggenheimer explains it along the same lines.
